predict.title: The order of calls
options: `after True`, `init`, `params` (the order they are written in)
predict.explanation: The order in the file doesn't matter: Blazor always calls **`OnInitialized`**, then **`OnParametersSet`**, then renders, then calls **`OnAfterRender`** with `firstRender` set to `true`.

predict.title: No loading state
options: Blazor waits 1 second, then shows the count
It shows **0 products**, then the real count after 1 second
A build error, because `products` can be `null`
predict.explanation:
When `OnInitializedAsync` awaits a task that is not finished, Blazor **renders right away**. At that moment `products` is still `null`, so `products.Count` throws a **`NullReferenceException`**. (The compiler only gives a nullable warning.) Add `@if (products is null) {

Loading...

}` before using it.

predict.title: Prerendering
options: Twice: once for the prerender, once when the page becomes interactive
Once per render of the page
predict.explanation: With prerendering, the server first renders the page to HTML with **one instance**. Then the interactive circuit creates a **new instance**, and its `OnInitialized` runs again. `OnInitialized` runs once **per instance**, and there are two instances.

predict.title: A timer with no re-render
options: An error, because the timer runs on another thread
predict.explanation: The field changes, but **nothing tells Blazor to render**. Blazor re-renders automatically after lifecycle methods and UI events, not after a timer callback. The callback should call `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`. Also, the timer is never disposed, so it keeps running after the component is removed.

practice.title: Reload when the parameter changes
practice.task:
On `/product/1`, the user clicks a link to `/product/2`. The URL changes, but the page keeps showing product 1: Blazor reused the same instance, so `OnInitializedAsync` did not run again.

Move the loading code to the method that runs **every time parameters are set**.

checks.label: No longer loads in `OnInitializedAsync`
checks.hint: Remove `OnInitializedAsync`: it runs only once per instance.

practice.title: JavaScript after the first render
practice.task:
This component reads the theme from `localStorage`. It crashes during prerendering, because there is no browser yet.

1. Move the JS call to **`OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)`**.
2. Run it **only on the first render**.
3. Call **`StateHasChanged()`** after you set `theme`, so the new value shows.
practice.hint: Changing a field in `OnAfterRenderAsync` doesn't render again by itself. That is why you call `StateHasChanged()`, and why it must be inside `if (firstRender)`.

checks.label: Overrides `OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)`
checks.hint: Add `protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)`.

checks.label: No JS call in `OnInitializedAsync`
checks.hint: Remove `OnInitializedAsync`: JS interop is not available during prerendering.

practice.title: Unsubscribe when the component is removed
practice.task:
`CartBadge` subscribes to `Cart.Changed`, but never unsubscribes. The cart service lives longer than the component, so it leaks.

1. Implement **`IDisposable`** with `@implements`.
2. Add **`public void Dispose()`** that unsubscribes with `-=`.
3. In the handler, use **`InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`**, because the event can fire on another thread.
practice.hint: The first line of the file is `@implements IDisposable`.

checks.label: `@implements IDisposable`
checks.hint: Add `@implements IDisposable` at the top of the file.

practice.title: A clock that ticks and stops
practice.task:
Fix this clock:

1. The timer callback must make the UI update: call **`InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`** after `seconds++`.
2. Implement **`IDisposable`** and **dispose the timer** in `Dispose`, so it stops when the component is removed.
practice.hint: Turn the lambda into a block: `_ => { seconds++; InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged); }`.

checks.label: The timer callback calls `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`
checks.hint: Inside the timer lambda, after `seconds++;`, add `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);`.

quiz.body: A child component has `[Parameter] public string Filter { get; set; }`. The parent changes the filter often. Which method runs **every time** the parent passes a new value?
quiz.explanation: `OnParametersSet{Async}` runs after every `SetParametersAsync`, so each time the parent passes parameters. `OnInitialized` runs only once per instance.

quiz.body: An AI tool wrote `await JS.InvokeVoidAsync("chart.draw", ...)` in `OnInitializedAsync` of a prerendered page. Where should it go?
quiz.explanation: JS interop needs a browser and the rendered elements. `OnAfterRender{Async}` runs after the render and is **not called during prerendering**, so it's the safe place. `firstRender` makes it run only once.

quiz.body: `OnInitializedAsync` does `items = await Api.GetItemsAsync();`, which takes 2 seconds. What happens during those 2 seconds?
options: The component renders once with `items` still unset, and renders again when the task finishes
Nothing is rendered until the task finishes
The component renders every 100 ms until the task finishes
The page shows an error until the task finishes
quiz.explanation: When the awaited task is not finished, Blazor **renders right away** with the current state, then renders again when it completes. That's why you start with `null` and show a loading state.

quiz.body: A page with `@rendermode InteractiveServer` and prerendering on loads its data in `OnInitializedAsync`. The database log shows **two** queries per visit. Why?
options: The browser requests the page twice
Two instances are created: one for the prerender on the server, one when the page becomes interactive
quiz.explanation: `OnInitialized{Async}` runs once **per instance**. Prerendering uses one instance to produce HTML, then the interactive circuit creates a new one. So the data loads twice unless you persist the prerendered state (Level 8).

quiz.body: A component implements both `IDisposable` and `IAsyncDisposable`. What does Blazor call when the component is removed?
quiz.explanation: If a component implements both interfaces, Blazor **only calls `DisposeAsync`**. Put all the cleanup there (or implement just one of them).

options: An endless loop: every render calls `OnAfterRender`, which asks for another render
It renders once more, then stops
A build error: `StateHasChanged` can't be called there
quiz.explanation: `StateHasChanged` schedules a render, and each render calls `OnAfterRender` again. Without an `if (firstRender)` guard (or another condition), it never stops.

quiz.body: A component overrides `protected override bool ShouldRender() => false;`. What happens?
options: The component never renders at all
It renders once (the first render), then skips every re-render
It renders only when `StateHasChanged` is called
It throws, because `ShouldRender` must return `true` at least once
quiz.explanation: `ShouldRender` is **not called for the first render**, so the component always renders once. After that, returning `false` skips re-renders, even after `StateHasChanged`.

quiz.body: A service raises an event from a background thread, and the component's handler needs to update the UI on Blazor Server. What should the handler call?
quiz.explanation: Code that runs outside Blazor (timers, service events) may be on another thread. `InvokeAsync` runs `StateHasChanged` on the component's own context. Calling it directly from another thread throws on the server.

quiz.body: What is the order of calls the **first** time a component is shown (interactive, no prerendering)?
quiz.explanation: Parameters arrive first (`SetParametersAsync`), then `OnInitialized{Async}`, then `OnParametersSet{Async}`, then the render, then `OnAfterRender{Async}(true)`.

quiz.body: A page has **no** interactive render mode (static SSR). It overrides `OnAfterRenderAsync` to log a message. When is the message logged?
options: Never: `OnAfterRender{Async}` is not called in static SSR
Once, after the HTML is sent
quiz.explanation: In static SSR (and during prerendering), the server only writes HTML. There is no browser and no interactive render, so `OnAfterRender{Async}` is **never called**.

interview.question: What are the main lifecycle methods of a Blazor component, in order?
interview.modelAnswer: `SetParametersAsync`, then `OnInitialized{Async}` (only the first time), then `OnParametersSet{Async}`, then the render, then `OnAfterRender{Async}` with `firstRender`. When the component is removed, `Dispose` or `DisposeAsync`. The sync version of each method runs before the async one.

interview.question: What is the difference between `OnInitialized` and `OnParametersSet`?
interview.modelAnswer: `OnInitialized` runs once per component instance, after the first parameters are set. `OnParametersSet` runs every time parameters are set, including the first time. Work that depends on a parameter that can change, like a route `Id`, belongs in `OnParametersSet`.

interview.question: Why does `OnInitializedAsync` sometimes run twice?
interview.modelAnswer: Because of prerendering. The server renders the page to HTML with one instance, then the page becomes interactive and a new instance is created, which runs `OnInitializedAsync` again. You can disable prerendering or persist the prerendered state to avoid loading twice.

interview.question: Why do pages that load data in `OnInitializedAsync` need a null check?
interview.modelAnswer: When the method awaits a task that isn't finished, Blazor renders right away with the current state, so the data is still `null` on the first render. The markup must check for `null` and show a loading state, then Blazor renders again when the data arrives.

interview.question: When and why do you use `OnAfterRender`?
interview.modelAnswer: After the component has rendered and its elements exist in the browser. It's the place for JS interop and for using `@ref` elements, like focusing an input. Use `firstRender` to do one-time setup. It isn't called during prerendering or static SSR.

interview.question: When do you need to call `StateHasChanged` yourself?
interview.modelAnswer: When state changes outside Blazor's normal flow: a timer, an event from a service, or after loading something in `OnAfterRenderAsync`. Blazor already re-renders after lifecycle methods and UI events. From another thread, call `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`.

interview.question: What does `ShouldRender` do?
interview.modelAnswer: It's called before each re-render. If it returns `false`, the re-render is skipped. It isn't called for the first render, so the component always renders at least once. It's used to avoid expensive renders when nothing visible changed.

interview.question: Why and how do you dispose a component?
interview.modelAnswer: To clean up anything that outlives it: unsubscribe from service events, dispose timers, and cancel pending work with a `CancellationTokenSource`. Otherwise you get leaks and code running for a removed component. Add `@implements IDisposable` and a `public void Dispose()` method, or `IAsyncDisposable` with `DisposeAsync` for async cleanup.
